text:
Match each item in Column A with its description in Column B.
Column A
(1) operator precedence
(2) a logical operator
(3) a relational operator
(4) an arithmetic operator
Column B
(a) The rule that decides which operators in an expression are applied first.
(b) An operator such as <, > or ==, which compares two values and gives a boolean.
(c) An operator such as &&, || or !, which works on boolean values.
(d) An operator such as +, −, *, / or %, which works on numbers.

points.text: (1) operator precedence goes with (a).
(2) a logical operator goes with (c).
(3) a relational operator goes with (b).
(4) an arithmetic operator goes with (d).

Column A
(1) an expression

(3) a literal
(4) an identifier
Column B
(a) A name given to a variable, method or class.
(b) A fixed value written directly in a program, such as 5 or "hi".
(c) A variable declared final, whose value can’t change after it’s set.
(d) A combination of values, variables and operators that gives a value.

points.text: (1) an expression goes with (d).
